answer: Each agent cures one cedar stack and reports its dawn moisture from a quartz meter. It locks an 80-credit bond, paying 41 for the first stack, 41+6(k-1) for the k-th; the 1000th costs 6035, so 1000 fakes pay 3,038,000 plus 80,000 locked. Auditors recompute the dawn moisture from the public cedar drying table and green weight, matching the quartz serial; deviation over 3 percent or a reused serial burns the bond. A rented-stack ring fails: one stack, one serial, one dawn reading, so a reused serial burns both bonds. An honest curer pays 41 once and redeems the bond after a clean epoch.
